reasons.reader_question: Clear hinge question: can they free the queen's guard when the queen is a live witness to every turning? The 'what will it cost Varanad' half stays faint.
reasons.change: Big knowledge shift: crown leaf confirmed, night-guard named as odiyans, Vellan arrives masterless. Neela moves from shelter to a purpose.
reasons.romance_movement: Shared purpose lands ('counting ahead, you taught me that'), but the beat's 'sworn in the open' partnership stays private and mostly restates ch 31's terms.
reasons.shown_chemistry: The 'whose three' count, the cups, and the cloth for Vellan are responsive. 'Felt the care in that as plainly as a hand on her back' narrates it.
reasons.character_logic: Refusing the flask and staying Thilak's knife fit Neela. Nobody notes that the watcher's log of their trail also reaches Chathu's buyers.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Costs are named: reading thirty pages adds witnesses, the queen finds them by new moon, and the season's resin runs out.
reasons.prose: Clean, varied and dash-free, but 'didn't say' recurs for Devan, 'twenty-two' is used three ways, and the queen's 'unfinished sentence' line is vague.
reasons.continuity: Vellan says thirty-one guards against the bible's thirty and his own 'thirty-first'. 40+30 is called seventy-one. Stubs move from the back half (F638) into the sealed quire.

fixes: 'Thirty-one, when I last counted' and 'Seventy-one?': continuity break. Make Vellan say 'Thirty. I'd have been the thirty-first,' and have Devan say 'Seventy. Seventy-one if Vellan stays.' Move the stubs back to the ledger's rear half. Neela opens the quire's sheet, then pulls the ledger from the pack and lays the thirty back-half stubs she already counted (F638) beside the list, so the match is the reveal.

'We'll need to start the plank': the beat asks for a partnership sworn in the open, which never happens. End with Neela and Devan carrying the plank out to the forty at the fire. Each says aloud what they will do for the thirty, as a shared purpose made before witnesses. Keep it short, two lines each, so it reads as a vow rather than a speech.

'I'm the only man in Varanad who'd walk it': character logic gap. If the watcher logged their trail, others can read it. Have Neela ask at once who else reads that log. Vellan answers that the log goes to Chathu's cell and then to whoever opens his post, so the clock to the new moon is real. Also cut 'she felt the care in that as plainly as a hand on her back' and let the basket act alone.
reader_question: Can Neela and Devan free the queen's thirty odiyan guards when the queen holds their pages and witnessed every first turning?
new_facts_assessment: Shelter, inventory and the carved bird are necessary and consistent; the spare flask fits Neela's flask going to the forty (F657). Problems: Vellan's 'thirty-one' guards conflicts with the bible's thirty guards and with his own 'I'd have been the thirty-first'. Putting the cut stubs inside the green-sealed front quire conflicts with F638, which places them in the back half and has Neela already counting them. Kamalakshi given age twenty-two echoes her ledger number and needs confirming. The bird 'smells of the sheds' sits awkwardly with Vellan carrying no resin scent.
